Question: A student claims: 'If two rectangles have the same perimeter, they must have the same area.' Is the claim true? Justify your answer. If it is false, give a counterexample using positive whole-number side lengths and calculate both perimeters and both areas.
Correct Answer: The claim is false. A 2 cm by 10 cm rectangle and a 4 cm by 8 cm rectangle both have perimeter 24 cm, but their areas are 20 and 32 square centimetres, respectively. Other valid counterexamples are possible.
Solution:
The claim is false. Consider a \(2\) cm by \(10\) cm rectangle and a \(4\) cm by \(8\) cm rectangle. Their perimeters are
\[P_1=2(2+10)=24\text{ cm}, \qquad P_2=2(4+8)=24\text{ cm}.\]
Their areas are
\[A_1=2\times10=20\text{ cm}^2, \qquad A_2=4\times8=32\text{ cm}^2.\]
These rectangles have equal perimeters and different areas, so they disprove the claim. A complete response must check both perimeters and show that the areas differ. Other valid examples also work.
